items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 2 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: You walked after some meals, which can help you see how it affects you. Walking after dinner is linked to a rise in sugar about 18.3 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: You had dinner before 8 pm most of the time, which is good. Having dinner at 8 pm or later is linked to sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You fasted for an average of 10.1 hours overnight. Fasting overnight is linked to some changes in blood sugar, but more research is needed to understand it.
